title: C. Raspberries
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan gave both the prime-k formula and the separate k = 4 branch with its three cases.
analysis_note: The code kept only the prime branch and dropped the entire k = 4 case, so composite k was handled by the wrong formula. It also used max instead of the min over (k - a_i mod k) that the plan specified, and it never triggered the zero-cost shortcut correctly because the loop indexes data without consuming it. Two independent deviations from an explicit plan, both on the implementation side.

title: B. 250 Thousand Tons of TNT
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan said to enumerate divisors by trial division up to sqrt(n) and explicitly to take both k and n // k.
analysis_note: The code enumerated only divisors k <= sqrt(n) and never added the paired divisor n // k, so most block sizes were never tested. It then tried to patch the k = n case by adding the whole array sum as a difference, which is not a difference of two truck loads at all and produced values like 4000000000. The plan's divisor rule was explicit, so this is a faithful-looking but incorrect realization.

title: Overall Winner
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan stated that on a tie the winner is the character that is NOT S[N-1].
analysis_note: The code implemented the tie-break in reverse, printing S[-1] itself as the winner. Every test with unequal counts passed (10/15) and only the tie cases failed, which pinpoints the inversion. The reasoning sentence explaining why the last-game winner reaches the count later was present in the plan but was not carried into the code.

title: Fill the Gaps
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified stepping +1 when A_i < A_{i+1} and -1 when A_i > A_{i+1}.
analysis_note: The code handles only the ascending direction: for a descending pair the expression range(diff - 1, 0, -1) with a negative diff is empty, so no values are inserted and the descending run disappears from the output. The sample already exposes this, giving 2 3 4 5 1 2 instead of the full sequence. One of the two branches the plan named was simply not written.

title: AtCoder Cards
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan required rejecting any letter outside {a, t, c, o, d, e, r} with a non-zero difference and required consuming the wildcard budgets cumulatively.
analysis_note: The code compares each letter's shortfall against the full wildcard count without ever deducting it, so several letters can each claim the same wildcards. It also omits the membership test for the seven allowed letters entirely, and ends with an unrelated check comparing the two wildcard totals. The plan named both constraints explicitly.

title: Bitmask
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified the all-zero base value followed by a most-significant-first greedy over the '?' positions.
analysis_note: The code never builds the base value from the fixed 0/1 characters, starts from float('inf'), walks the '?' positions from the least significant end, and prints -1 as soon as any bit would exceed N. The resulting procedure has no relation to the planned greedy and scores 0/15. This is a case where the plan was concrete and the generated algorithm was still different.

title: Pac
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified BFS from the start, the goal and each candy, then dp[mask][i] over at most 18 candies.
analysis_note: The BFS pushes ((row, col), 0) but unpacks three values, so it crashes on the first pop. The dp function is also structurally wrong: it indexes dp[mask][mask], references an undefined distances variable and an undefined T, and uses a Candy class defined after its first use. The plan's two-stage structure was not realized at any level, which matches the pattern of hard problems exceeding the 3B model's implementation capacity.

title: Anti
missing_or_wrong_information: None algorithmically. The plan's three-phase DP was verified against brute force on all three samples before use.
analysis_note: The code writes S[i] - 'A' as if characters were C chars, which raises a TypeError immediately in Python. Structurally it also repeats the same phase-0 loop three times over the whole string instead of carrying one left-to-right pass through the phases, and it never implements the fixed-uppercase symmetry split or the modular inverse. This plan is the densest of the 50 and is a plausible upper bound on what a 3B model can follow.

title: Find snuke
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified scanning every 's' cell over the 8 direction vectors and checking the next four cells for n, u, k, e.
analysis_note: The code passes sys.stdin.read() into a function that then calls input() again, so the stream is already exhausted and it dies with EOFError. The direction scan itself is also wrong: it compares against chr(ord('n') + step), which spells n, o, p, q rather than n, u, k, e. The plan's search structure was followed but both the I/O and the target letters were mishandled.

title: Isolation
missing_or_wrong_information: The initial value of the isolated-vertex counter. All N vertices start with no edges, so the counter must be initialized to N; the plan only said to maintain 'a counter of vertices whose set is empty' and never stated its starting value.
analysis_note: The code follows the plan almost line by line: adjacency sets, decrement on insertion into an empty set, the clearing loop with increments, and buffered output. Its only defect is empty_count = 0 at the start, which makes every printed value exactly N too small, and the observed output -2, -3, -3, ... for N = 3 confirms precisely that offset. High fidelity to an under-specified plan makes this the one genuine planning failure among these 26 cases.

title: Merge Set
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified the set-value bipartite graph and a 0-1 BFS with a deque, cost 1 entering a set and 0 leaving one.
analysis_note: The code reads each set element with its own input() call although the elements share one line, so it crashes on the first set. Beyond that, it uses a plain BFS with uniform cost instead of the 0-1 deque BFS, mixes value indices and set indices in one graph array without an offset for values, and marks visited[0] instead of the start value. The planned cost model was not implemented.

title: Dash
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified maintaining the current position, decrementing health per move, the negative-health stop, and consuming an item only when health < K.
analysis_note: The code never maintains a position: it resets x, y to (H, 0) inside every iteration, so the coordinate it looks up is derived from the remaining health rather than from the walk. Health and the x coordinate are also conflated in the same variable H. The item and threshold logic was copied from the plan, but the simulation state it operates on is meaningless.

title: Shift vs. CapsLock
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan gave the transition new_dp[s] = min over s' of dp[s'] + (Z if s != s' else 0) + typing cost.
analysis_note: The code drops the minimum entirely and always takes the value from the opposite state, so staying in the same Caps Lock state is never considered and a toggle cost is added on almost every character. It also decides the toggle by comparing the character rather than the state pair. The sample already gives 17 instead of 9, and only the single-character case passes.

title: First Player
failure_type: Wrong Answer / Type Error in Comparison
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan stated that ages are compared as plain integers and that output starts from the youngest with modulo wrap.
analysis_note: The code stores the age as the raw string from split() and takes min() over (age, name) tuples, so ages are compared lexicographically and '31' sorts before '5'. The cyclic printing that follows is exactly as planned, which is why 5/14 tests still pass. A one-token int() conversion separates this code from a full pass.

title: Virus
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified squared-distance comparison against D*D and a BFS from person 1 over the resulting components.
analysis_note: The algorithm is implemented exactly as planned, including the integer squared-distance test that avoids square roots. The only defect is the input line X, Y = [list(...) for _ in range(N)], which tries to unpack N coordinate rows into two names and raises a ValueError for any N != 2. This is a pure parsing bug on top of a faithful implementation.

title: A Piece of Cake
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified bisect on the sorted cut lines, a dictionary keyed by cell, and the rule that the minimum is 0 when some cell is empty.
analysis_note: The counting logic, the dictionary choice over a dense table, and the empty-cell rule all follow the plan. The failure is the input line A, a = map(int, input().split()), sorted(...), which binds A to a map object, so (A + 1) * (B + 1) raises a TypeError. Reading A and B as single integers on their own lines would make this code pass.

title: Good Graph
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified building the DSU over the given edges first, then mapping the K forbidden pairs to component roots.
analysis_note: The code defines find and union but never creates the parent and size arrays, so the first find call raises a NameError. It also collects the M edges into a list and never unions them, meaning the component structure the plan is built on would be missing even if the arrays existed. The query logic itself matches the plan exactly.

title: Sleep Log
missing_or_wrong_information: None, though the plan's phrasing of P as one entry per index of A invited a compressed variant.
analysis_note: The code builds P with one entry per sleep session (length about N/2) but then indexes it with k obtained from bisect over the full array A, which runs off the end. Its parity test is also shifted: the plan specified adding t - A_k when k is even in 1-indexed terms, and the code tests k % 2 == 0 on a 0-indexed k, which is the opposite set of positions. Both defects are index-base handling rather than algorithm choice.

title: Art Gallery on Graph
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified per-vertex adjacency lists and relaxing each neighbour with h - 1 from a max-heap.
analysis_note: The code never builds adjacency lists and instead scans the whole edge list on every pop, treating any edge whose first endpoint differs from the current vertex as a neighbour. That is both O(M) per pop, which times out, and semantically wrong, since it relaxes unrelated vertices; the smaller tests show a wrong vertex set as well. The relaxation rule and the best >= 0 output condition came straight from the plan.

title: Centers
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified two arrays of size N, a per-value counter and the recorded middle index.
analysis_note: The code uses a defaultdict of lists and then overwrites the list with a bare integer once the second occurrence is seen, so the third occurrence calls append on an int and raises an AttributeError. The sorting key that follows is exactly the planned one. Using the two plain arrays the plan named would have avoided the type change entirely.

title: Poisonous Full
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan stated that an antidotal course leads to the healthy state from either previous state, and that skipping keeps both states.
analysis_note: The code implements healthy = max(healthy, upset + Y) and omits the healthy + Y branch, so eating an antidotal course while already healthy is never counted. On the third sample this loses exactly the two positive antidotal courses and yields 3900000000 instead of 4100000000. One transition out of the three the plan listed is missing.

title: Best Performances
failure_type: Runtime Error + Timeout / Malformed Fenwick Tree
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified a Fenwick tree carrying both counts and sums over compressed ranks, plus a descending walk for the K-th largest.
analysis_note: The code builds only a count tree with no sum tree, so the planned answer formula cannot be evaluated. It also compresses ranks from the all-zero initial array, giving a single rank, and then calls update with the raw value Y as an index, which runs past the end of the tree and raises an IndexError on test 0; larger tests exhaust the time limit instead, which is why the aggregate status is TIMEOUT. The K-th largest search is a plain binary search over prefix counts rather than the descending tree walk the plan specified.

title: Ideal Sheet
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified normalizing each sheet's black cells to its bounding box and enumerating placements of those boxes inside X.
analysis_note: The code skips the normalization step and shifts the raw coordinates over the ad hoc range(-H_X + 1, H_A + 1), which neither covers all valid placements nor stays inside X. Its early fit check also compares raw maxima against H_X and W_X, rejecting sheets whose black cells sit far from the origin. 14/16 tests still pass because most placements happen to fall inside the scanned range.

title: Default Price
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan warned explicitly that the price line holds M+1 values with P_0 first and that this is easy to misalign.
analysis_note: The code slices colors as data[2:N+2] and then treats everything after it as prices, which still contains the M colour names D_i, so int() raises a ValueError on the first of them. It also zips the eaten plates with prices instead of building the map from D to P. The warning the plan carried was the exact failure that occurred.

title: Standings
failure_type: Wrong Answer / Wrong Tie-Break and 0-Indexed Output
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan specified exact rational comparison, descending by rate, and ascending by index on ties.
analysis_note: The code adopts the plan's exact Fraction comparison but sorts the (rate, index) tuples with reverse=True, which also reverses the index order and breaks ties backwards. It additionally prints the 0-based loop variable instead of the 1-based person number, so every line is off by one and all 15 tests fail. Sorting by (-rate, index) would fix both aspects of the ordering.

title: Snuke Maze
missing_or_wrong_information: None. The plan stated that the letter fixes the position in the s, n, u, k, e cycle and that the start must be checked for 's'.
analysis_note: The code derives the next required letter as chr(ord('a') + (ord(c) - ord('a') + 1) % 5), which maps letters through the alphabet instead of through the word snuke, so almost no legal move is accepted. It also never verifies that (1,1) holds 's' before starting. The BFS skeleton and the visited-grid argument came from the plan unchanged.
